# c06 - SUYU-GURecomp facts vs. MHGU 1.4.0 disassembly

Source: SUYU-GURecomp commit 35015f1, `game_settings.cpp` lines 1206-1207 (message-handling routine body). Address convention: SUYU "main+X" equals our vaddr X.

| vaddr | meaning | SUYU cite | status | evidence |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0x139e71c | Interior dispatch point of the message routine, not a routine entry: it tests a pointer held in a frame slot (`[r11]`), calls `0x13a88c4` with the context in r10 when non-null, keeps the result in r7, then re-tests a second object reached through `[sp, #16]` and, when that too is non-null, calls `0x13a63ac(r9)` followed by `0x13a6d94` which builds its output in place at `sp+20` from `[[sp, #12]]`, r7, r9 | game_settings.cpp:1206 | PLAUSIBLE | `0139e71c: e59b0000  ldr r0, [r11, #0]` / `0139e72c: eb002864  bl 0x13a88c4` / `0139e764: e28d0014  add r0, sp, #20` - frame-relative locals and no prologue in the window, so mid-function; nothing contradicts a line attribution there, but the address cannot be an entry |
| 0x139e730 | Return-value handoff immediately after the `0x13a88c4` call: r0 (the call result) is moved into r7 and tested; on null it jumps forward to the failure branch `0x139e79c`, otherwise it dereferences `[sp, #16]` and tests that object's first member, choosing between `0x139e7b8` and the path that calls `0x13a63ac(r9)` and then `0x13a6d94` | game_settings.cpp:1207 | PLAUSIBLE | `0139e730: e1a07000  mov r7, r0` / `0139e738: 0a000017  beq 0x139e79c` - a plain register move plus a conditional branch of the enclosing routine, i.e. mid-statement/mid-function; no push, no new frame, so it is a line-level boundary at best, not an entry |
| 0x139e76c | Result check of the preceding `0x13a6d94` call: loads the object it built at `sp+20`; when non-null it performs an indirect virtual call through `[r10] -> [8]` with this=r10, r2=0x08000000 and r3=0, then calls `0x13a6464(r9)` and branches to `0x139e7d0`; when null it falls through to `0x139e7f8` | game_settings.cpp:1207 | PLAUSIBLE | `0139e76c: e59d0014  ldr r0, [sp, #20]` / `0139e78c: e12fff31  blx r1` - same-line duplicate of the 0x139e730 block: a frame-slot load and an indirect call inside the routine body, no prologue, so the address is interior code and only the line mapping is under test |
